source_text: His peractis Machabaico gaudio Mariani mater exultans et passione perfecta iam secura de filio, non illi tantum coeperat, sed et sibi, quae tale pignus ediderat, gratulari. Conplectebatur in filii corpore suorum uiscerum gloriam, et in ipsa ceruicis uulnera frequens osculum pietas religiosa figebat. O te merito Mariam! O te beatam et filio tuo, mater, et nomine! Quis in ea tanti uocabuli felicitatem aliquando credat errasse, quam sic uteri sui fetus ornauit? Inaestimabilis uere dei omnipotentis et Christi eius in suos misericordia, qui fidentes in suum nomen non solum gratiae dignatione confortat, sed et sanguinis redemptione uiuificat. Nam quis digna aestimatione possit eius beneficia metiri? Qui in hoc quoque paterna indulgentia semper operatur, ut in nos et hoc ipsum, quod in nostro sanguine rependi credimus, conferatur ab omnipotente deo; cui est gloria in saecula saeculorum, amen.
pass_a_gloss: These things having been done, with Maccabean joy the mother of Marianus exulting and now free from anxiety about her son, his suffering having been completed, began to congratulate not him only but also herself who had brought forth such a pledge; she was embracing in the body of her son the glory of her own womb, and religious devotion was fixing frequent kisses upon the very wounds of his neck; O you deservedly Mary, O blessed mother both in your son and in your name, who could ever believe the fortune of so great a name had failed in her whom the offspring of her womb so adorned; truly inestimable is the mercy of omnipotent God and his Christ toward his own, who strengthens those trusting in his name not only by the condescension of grace but makes alive by redemption of blood; for who could measure his benefits with worthy measure, who also in this always works with paternal kindness so that even this which we believe is repaid in our blood is conferred upon us by omnipotent God, to whom is glory unto ages of ages, amen.
pass_b_english: When these things were accomplished, the mother of Marianus, exulting with Maccabean joy and now at peace concerning her son because his passion had been brought to completion, began to congratulate not him alone but also herself, who had brought forth such a pledge. She embraced in her son's body the glory of her own womb, and with holy devotion she pressed repeated kisses upon the very wounds of his neck. O you rightly called Mary! O mother blessed both in your son and in your name! Who could ever believe that the good fortune of so great a name had gone astray in her, whom the fruit of her womb so adorned?

Truly inestimable is the mercy of almighty God and of his Christ toward his own, who strengthens those who trust in his name not only by the condescension of grace but also gives them life by the redemption of blood. For who could measure his benefits with a worthy measure? For in this also he ever works with fatherly kindness, so that even what we believe we repay in our own blood is itself bestowed on us by almighty God, to whom be glory for ever and ever, amen (Galatians 1:5).
